sections.title: Asset Quality
sections.subtitle: Non-performing assets and provisioning -- the credit-risk side of the lending book

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For ICICI Bank Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For ICICI Bank Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nim.title: Net interest margin
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the core profitability metric of a lender; a few basis points move earnings materially.

What to watch:

  • NIM trend with the rate cycle
  • Funding cost versus lending yield

casa.title: CASA ratio
casa.content:
The CASA ratio is current + savings account deposits as a percentage of total deposits -- a bank's cheapest, stickiest source of funding. Period-end is the balance on the reporting date; the quarterly average smooths out the point-in-time window-dressing that inflates the period-end figure.

For ICICI Bank Limited: a wide gap between the two series, or a period-end print well above the average, signals deposit mobilisation timed around the reporting date rather than a durable improvement in funding cost.

What to watch:

  • Average CASA drifting down even if period-end holds up
  • CASA ratio against peers -- it is the main structural driver of NIM

npaRatios.title: Gross and net NPA ratio
npaRatios.content:
Gross NPA ratio is non-performing advances as a percentage of total advances, before provisions. Net NPA ratio deducts provisions already held against those loans -- the residual credit risk still on the balance sheet.

For ICICI Bank Limited: both ratios fell from above 7% in FY2018 to near 1% by FY2026 as the corporate-lending stress cycle (steel, infrastructure) that peaked mid-decade worked through the book; the direction matters more than any single quarter.

What to watch:

  • Gross NPA rising even one or two quarters in a row -- it leads net NPA and provisioning
  • The gap between gross and net widening (under-provisioning) or narrowing (balance sheet clean-up)
  • Slippage concentrated in one segment (retail, corporate, agri) disclosed in the filing's asset-quality note

provisionCoverage.title: Provision coverage ratio
provisionCoverage.content:
The provision coverage ratio (PCR) is total provisions held against non-performing assets, as a percentage of gross NPAs. A higher PCR means more of the bad-loan risk is already absorbed through the P&L rather than left as a future charge.

For ICICI Bank Limited: management built PCR up into the 80s during FY2019-FY2021 ahead of the pandemic, then let it drift back toward the mid-70s as gross NPAs themselves fell -- a lower ratio against a shrinking, cleaner NPA pool is not the same signal as a falling ratio against a growing one.

What to watch:

  • PCR falling at the same time gross NPA is rising -- the combination that precedes a credit-cost shock
  • PCR relative to the regulatory floor and to peer banks

nta.title: NTA per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is net tangible assets divided by shares -- the book value of the portfolio.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the share price relative to NTA is the market's view of the portfolio's valuation and management.

What to watch:

  • Discount or premium to NTA
  • NTA growth from revaluations versus retained cash

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For ICICI Bank Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

totalIncome.title: Total income
totalIncome.content:
Net interest income plus fees and other operating income.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the top line for a financial; revenue in the ordinary sense does not apply.

What to watch:

  • Income growth versus cost growth
